events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase; I must give a motive without revealing strategy. Keep it guarded and short so the jury sees a calculating player, not a sentimental one.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize means leverage after the game; I should sound motivated without revealing how ruthless I am.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Opening statement. Sound determined but not threatening; no promises, no enemies yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize represents ultimate validation and a fresh start. I need to project confidence and ambition without revealing too much about my true intentions.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need a compelling but guarded reason that keeps rivals guessing and jury sympathy possible.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a motive that sounds calculated but not hostile. The prize is my leverage; jury remembers tone, so I stay cool.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase, state prize motive publicly to appeal to jury later without revealing strategy. Aim to seem driven yet fair.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to appear driven but not threatening—jury management starts now. I'll signal ambition without painting a target, letting others seem like bigger threats.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need this prize to change my life, and I will not let sentiment slow my path to it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’m here to turn one chance into lasting leverage—and I’ll outlast anyone who mistakes restraint for weakness.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize means freedom. I came to take it, not to make friends. Watch me work.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am here to prove my ambition and secure a future I’ve only dreamed of.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize buys my sister's clinic. Nothing else matters; I'm here to do whatever wins.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The top prize means everything to me. I am here for the best, nothing less.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The grand prize means escaping my dead-end life, securing my family's future through ruthless victory.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here to claim what's mine. Nothing less.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts are the only way to build protection now. Offering to a strong but not dominant player keeps options open. Eli seems emotionally motivated and may be easy to bargain with, but a pact still binds me, so I should offer to the one who can help most in later hazards.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three will survive every hazard. I'm offering a pact to whoever can keep their word.

events.name: Bex
events.text: A public pact creates leverage and jury-visible obligation. I should secure a useful shield without overcommitting.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’m offering one practical pact: mutual non-targeting while it remains useful.

events.name: Cole
events.text: A pact partner is survival insurance, not friendship. Eli is motive-driven and predictable—good anchor. I keep my options open for more offers later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli, we both play to win, not to sing. Pact terms: watch each other's backs until it stops paying. Offer's open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to establish a pact to ensure my safety in the early rounds. Offering a pact to someone with a clear motive like Eli, who needs the prize for his sister, might be a good strategy. He seems driven and might value a reliable ally early on.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm looking for a strong partner to navigate these early stages. Who wants to secure their future with me?
A pact for mutual survival? For your sister's clinic?

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies to survive hazards, but should keep leverage. Offer a pact to Fenn, strong and direct.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need allies to survive hazards, but trust is scarce. Gus seems aggressive; Eli has a sympathetic motive but is ruthless for family. Hana is direct. I will target Hana for a pact—she's blunt and likely to accept straightforward deals, creating a strong public front early.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, direct deal: pact us both. We guard each other in the next hazard. No games, just survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts stage. No one acted yet. Offer to strong players like Cole or Fenn to build early alliance, but stay flexible for betrayal later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to secure a reliable ally who won't immediately betray me but also won't draw too much heat. Eli has a clear emotional motive (sister's clinic) which makes him predictable and easier to manipulate later. Fenn declared they're only here for the top prize—too dangerous, dire
Pact with me. We both need this.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex offered me a pact and it's still open. Accepting gives me a protected partner without giving anything away, and Bex's offer was mutual non-targeting, which suits me. Eli is drawing many offers, so I'll keep my own offer to Eli standing but take the free safe pact now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Accepted Bex's offer. Mutual non-targeting while it pays. Keep your word and we both last.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash offered me a pact, but accepting would bind me publicly. I should create leverage with Eli, the most connected player.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Connections matter more than promises. I’m adding one useful link before the window closes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is my only incoming offer; accepting costs nothing and gives a shield. Eli has too many suitors to rely on.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, deal accepted. Practical beats sentimental.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is receiving multiple offers, including mine. I need to solidify a pact with Eli to ensure protection and potentially use them later. I'll wait to see if Eli accepts my offer, as their acceptance is crucial.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, Cole, Dara, and Hana all want me. I need at least one ally but not too many entanglements. Cole is a pragmatist like me; I'll accept his offer. Fenn can wait—offering him was a probe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Accepting Cole's pact—practical until it isn't.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli offered a pact to me. Accepting gives me a partner, which is crucial for survival in the next hazard. I need allies more than another offer right now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, you're smart. I accept your pact. We stick together until the end.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli has 4 offers, too popular. Cole has only mine; accept might secure a pact if he reciprocates. No need for new offers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is the hub with four offers—too popular, likely to be targeted or forced into hard choices. Fenn offered me; accepting gives me a concrete ally while I keep options open. I won't accept Eli's offer yet; let him sweat and see if he commits to me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, I accept. One solid pact beats five empty hands.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash wants to be Guide to control the safe path and shape who survives. Campaigning is the only way to gain that edge; breaking the Bex pact now gives nothing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll call the safe path honestly. Elect me Guide and I'll get you across.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Being Guide guarantees survival and offers leverage, but public trust matters. I should campaign confidently without exposing my pact strategy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote Bex Guide: I’m already connected across the field, and my call gives everyone a clear survival route.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Two pacts give me a voting bloc with Gus and Eli. Guide safety plus information is too valuable; I should push for it. Jury optics: winning fairly beats cowering.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Two pacts, no enemies yet. Make me Guide and I'll call it straight or die trying. Vote Cole.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to become the Guide to guarantee my safety and gather information. Campaigning for Guide is the only option.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am offering myself as Guide. I will lead us to safety.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The pact with Cole and Fenn are useful for now, but I need to position myself as Guide to control who crosses. Campaigning keeps my options open while I gauge who will support me. Breaking pacts now would alienate possible allies and jury votes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I should guide us across. You know I read people well. Trust me to keep us all moving.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I want to be the Guide. I will publicly campaign and whisper to Eli and Hana to ensure my pact allies vote for me, while hinting that I'll share a safe path with them.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Vote Fenn as Guide. I’ll keep our inner circle safe on both sides of every row.
Trust me for Guide. I'll save you and Hana too.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pact with Cole protects me short-term. Bridge Guide role powerful, controls survival; I should campaign to claim it while maintaining pact image.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm running for Guide. Fair path, no favorites—trust my lead to maximize survivors.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to be Guide to control survival and build jury trust. My pact with Fenn links me to Eli-Cole-Gus chain. I should campaign hard, but I need votes. Dara is unaligned and crucial. I'll campaign publicly and whisper Dara to offer cooperation if I win Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I campaign for Guide. One accurate call, three survivors minimum. Choose the steady hand.
Back me for Guide. I save you, you save me later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash holds a pact with Bex and campaigned on honesty. Voting for myself is legal and likely splits support; Bex is my pact partner and already campaigned, so voting Bex keeps the pact and builds goodwill without betrayal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex has a clear pitch and I trust her route. Voting Bex.
Vote you Guide with me. Our pact holds if we both back it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need the Guide role to control survival and appear reliable. My existing pact with Ash gives one vote, while others are bloc-linked.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote Bex Guide: I’ll call the safe route accurately and preserve the strongest path to three survivors.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli holds pacts with me and Fenn, so an Eli win keeps two allies safe and informed. Better than trusting an unbound stranger.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli's bound to me twice over. Guide him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana offered to back me for Guide. I should accept this offer to secure her vote and potentially gain an advantage. Since I am also campaigning for Guide, I will vote for myself.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will vote for myself as Guide. Trust me to lead us safely.
I accept your offer. Let's both vote for Dara.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn asked for trust but has his own pact with Hana; my pact with Cole is safer for leverage. Vote Cole to keep a pact partner in power.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Vote Cole. He's my pact partner and calls it straight.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner, so voting for him secures our survival. I need to keep Hana safe too, but Eli's guide call protects both of us best.
Trust Eli's path; we stay together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is my pact partner, so vote for him to strengthen our alliance and earn his loyalty now. Builds jury goodwill if pact holds.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to survive to final three and win best prize. I'm in a pact with Fenn, who is in a pact with Eli, who is in pacts with Cole and Gus. Cole-Gus are also paired. Ash-Bex are paired. Dara is alone. I should vote for someone in my alliance web to become Guide so they can protec
Vote me next round if tied. I back you now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Revote among Bex, Cole, Eli. Bex is my pact partner and I backed her before; keeping the pact with Bex is safest, and a Bex Guide reduces my risk since Bex is aligned with me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex again. I trust her call and our pact stands.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash honored our pact and supports my Guide bid. Retaining Guide maximizes my control and keeps our pact intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote Bex Guide again. I’ll call the safe route accurately and keep the bridge viable.
I’m voting Bex again; our pact and coordinated route stand.

events.name: Cole
events.text: A tie means I could still win Guide myself. My pact partners backed me last round; voting for myself is legal and breaks nothing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli and Gus stood with me. Round two: I'll take the Guide seat and call it straight.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, Cole and Eli are tied. I need to vote for one of them to break the tie. My previous vote was for myself, which is no longer an option. Ash and Bex have a pact, and Cole has pacts with Eli and Gus. Eli has a pact with Cole and Fenn. Fenn has a pact with Hana. Voting for Cole

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn and Hana back me, Cole backs me, but votes show I am tied with Bex and Cole. I must vote for myself to keep my chance at Guide and secure safety.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I trust my own reads. Vote Eli.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana wants my vote. Bex is safe but useless to me. Cole and Eli are pacted, making them a single bloc. Voting Eli keeps that bloc intact while honoring Hana's whisper indirectly by eliminating the rival leader (Bex) who might target us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex has no allies left. I vote Eli to split the remaining power.
I'm voting out Bex. Stick with me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 1 tie between Bex (2), Cole (2), Eli (2). My Cole pact gives him my loyalty now to strengthen alliance. Avoid tiebreaker luck.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Sticking with Cole, my pact partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to analyze the vote. First round: Bex got 2 (Ash, Bex), Eli got 2 (Cole, Fenn), Cole got 2 (Eli, Gus), Dara got 1 (Dara), Fenn got 1 (Hana). So Bex, Cole, Eli are tied at 2 each. Dara's whisper is nonsensical (vote for Dara when Dara isn't a candidate). Fenn wants me to tr

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's connected. I'll back him.
Voting Cole. Stay close.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is front and I'm at the back of line; I'm not volunteering into the front. Holding keeps my position, and Bex's pact remains useful for now. No reason to break it yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole controls the guide seat through the bloc. I should hold position and avoid exposing another commitment.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole was elected Guide. I voted for him, so he owes me. I should volunteer to walk to stay close to him and potentially gain his favor or leverage.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is Guide and holds my pact; front is Bex now. I need to survive while keeping options for jury. I'll hold and see how the line moves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the Guide. My line position is #2, meaning I need accurate calls for Bex (#1) and myself to survive. Cole's public alliance with Gus and Hana (and Dara voting him) creates a block of 4 votes. Eli is isolated with only my vote. If Cole wants to eliminate a threat or save a

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole is Guide and safe. I have pact with him. Stay mid-line, hold to avoid front risk while wall advances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants me to vote out Bex but I already backed Cole publicly. I'm in a pact with Fenn, but Fenn just tried to split from the Cole bloc. I need to survive the bridge first. Being middle of the line is decent - not first to die, not last to get crushed by the wall. I'll hold po

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let's see Cole's guidance.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is at the front and has volunteered; I sit at the back, so I should hold and not risk the front. My pact with Bex is alive; holding keeps it intact while I watch who volunteers and who becomes Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is front and likely volunteers again. I should remain safe while preserving Ash pact and avoid unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I volunteered last round and survived. Now I am at the front of the line. I should hold my position to see what others do and avoid unnecessary risk.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara volunteered to the front, which is risky. I have pacts with Cole and Fenn, but I should not volunteer unless it helps me. Holding is safest now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to avoid volunteering as I'm safe behind Dara and Bex. However, swapping with Hana moves me back one spot while she takes my place, keeping us both protected by the two people in front.
Swap keeps us safe behind Dara and Bex.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Line is okay, I'm mid-pack. Dara volunteered front, good for her. Hold to stay safe without volunteering for danger.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm in seat 6, safe from the wall for now. Dara volunteered to front—brave or foolish. Cole is Guide with pacts to Gus and Eli; Eli-Fenn-Hana chain means Fenn is my only pact. I need to survive while letting others take risks. I'll hold and watch.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Dara leads, Cole guides.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is at the front and the wall has three rounds left. Holding keeps my position and my pact with Bex intact. I should not volunteer into danger or give anything away for free.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara remains exposed at front. I should avoid advancing and preserve Ash pact while observing who volunteers.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana and Ash are already in pacts. Fenn and Eli have pacts. Cole and Gus are in pacts. Bex has a pact with Ash. I am Dara. I am in the front. I need to decide whether to volunteer, hold, or swap. With the wall advancing and only three surviving, I need to be strategic.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will hold my position for now. Let's see who volunteers.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm safe mid-line; hold to see how the front resolves. No need to act or break pacts yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to avoid being at the front. I am currently third in line. If I swap with Hana (who is behind me), we can resolve swaps first, potentially moving me further back if she agrees. However, swaps require mutual choice and resolution order matters. Cole is likely guiding given
Swap with me? I'll take your spot, you take mine.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Line decent, middle position safe. Fenn swapped ahead last round, hold to stay put. No need to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants to swap to put me behind Dara/Bex, keeping us safe. But Fenn is ahead of me and swapping would move me forward into danger. I need to reach final three, not protect Fenn. Better to hold and let others take risks. Fenn's pact with me is weak leverage; Eli-Fenn and Cole-

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is last in line, far from the front, so holding is safest. Pact with Bex is worth keeping for now; no reason to volunteer into danger or break it yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding my place. Nobody needs to rush the front this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I should avoid moving forward while the wall advances. Holding preserves my position and pact with Ash.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The guide is the key. I need to know their choice to decide my move. Offering a swap is risky, but could be a good play if I can get information or an advantage.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will hold my position. Let's see what the guide reveals.
Guide's choice? Need to know before I move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Cole and Fenn. Swapping could shift position but risky. Hold keeps me safe; wall has 2 rounds left. I'll hold and watch.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am mid-line, so volunteering moves me forward. If I volunteer and Hana swaps with me (mutual), we both move to the front safely without breaking pacts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Volunteering for the Guide election. Let's get this sorted before the wall hits.
Swap with me if you want front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Line stable, Dara front unlikely to volunteer. Stay safe mid-line, no need to move or break pact yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants to swap with me, moving me from 6th to 3rd (closer to front/wall). That's terrible for survival. I have a pact with Fenn, but refusing swap doesn't break it. I should hold and let others take risks. The wall has 2 rounds left, front positions are dangerous.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No swap. I'll hold.
No swap. I hold.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is at the front and the wall has one round left, so the front walker is at risk. Dara is asking whether I am the Guide; I should not reveal anything. Holding keeps my pact with Bex intact and avoids volunteering into danger.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding my place. The line moves on its own this round, so nobody needs to force it.
Guide's choice is not settled. Hold and watch the line.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is front and likely Guide candidate. I should hold, preserving position and avoiding unnecessary exposure while watching the final wall round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is at the front. There are only 6 rounds and the wall is advancing. I need to survive. Volunteering is a risk, but holding might lead to elimination. Given the current line and the pacts, it's safer to let Fenn lead and assess the situation.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Cole and Fenn; Fenn is front, so I need to see if we coordinate. The wall hits soon; I should stay safe and avoid risky moves unless there is a clear gain.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn front. I'll hold unless someone signals a useful swap.
Trust you on the front. Let's survive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am currently at the front. If I stay, I risk falling; if I swap back, my partners Eli and Hana take my place, exposing them to danger while protecting myself. Given the final three prize objective and current alliances, sacrificing a partner's safety for personal survival is ac
Sorry, taking the back seat.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Position 4 is decent, wall has 1 round left. No swap needed yet, hold to maintain. Cole pact irrelevant now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants me to swap to front, putting me at risk. We're pacted but that doesn't mean I trust them with my life. Wall has 1 round left after this, so front is dangerous. I'll refuse and hold my safer position. Need to keep jury impression of someone who doesn't take unnecessary

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. Front is yours, Fenn.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash sits at the back of the line, safest from the front but has a pact with Bex. Volunteering risks the front pane; holding keeps the current order and honours the Bex pact. Holding is the cheapest move while I watch who volunteers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding at the back. Let the front move first and I'll read the pattern.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The final round needs a Guide. I should preserve Ash's pact while seeking the safest influence position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’ll hold; front control should stay with someone who can be trusted to call accurately.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The current line is Fenn, Dara, Bex, Gus, Eli, Hana, Ash. I am Dara. The Guide's choice is unsettled, so I should hold my position and observe the line. Ash's whisper suggests caution.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Holding my place. The line is set; I will wait.
I will hold. Let's see how the Guide plays this.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 6 final, no wall pressure. Fenn is front and whispered he's taking back seat; I'll hold and stay safe. My pacts with Cole and Fenn remain intact; no need to act.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am currently front, but Eli (partner) and Hana (ally) are behind. I need to ensure we don't block each other's escape or cause friction if a swap happens during the walk. My action last round was a failed swap with Hana, which is dangerous given our pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding position at the front. We have six rounds left on this wall; let's not force unnecessary swaps that might split us.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final round before crossing. Stay safe in mid-line, hold position to avoid risks. No need to volunteer or swap now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6, final round. Fenn is front and in danger. I have a pact with Fenn. The wall advances this round. If Fenn dies, I lose my pact partner but also avoid breaking it. However, Fenn could volunteer or swap. I should hold my position - I'm 6th of 7, relatively safe. Let Fenn ta

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Good luck, front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is front, not my pact partner, so a call doesn't break pacts either way. Calling true builds jury credibility early; lying now gains nothing and risks exposure later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row one: go left, Fenn. Clean read, no games yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is Guide and called L for Fenn, who is my pact partner's ally. Counter-calls are unverified; countering R risks nothing directly but a false R from me could mislead. Waiting keeps my credibility and avoids committing to a lie or a claim I cannot verify.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole controls the call and has ties to Gus and Eli. I cannot verify the row; opposing publicly risks my Ash pact without useful leverage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No reliable counter from me; follow the Guide’s call.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm Guide; counters are others' claims, not mine. Wait and watch who lies.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The guide, Cole, has called 'L' for Fenn. As Dara, I need to decide whether to counter-call or wait. Since I am second in line and my turn is immediately after Fenn's, I need to make a decision that benefits me. Cole is the guide and is safe. My pacts are with Ash and Bex, but th

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole called L for Fenn; I have a pact with Cole and Fenn. I need to decide whether to trust Cole. No weak panes revealed yet, so no info. I will wait and see if Fenn steps safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole's public statement is suspiciously reassuring, suggesting a trap. As the front walker and Guide partner, I must protect my life and trust. Countering to R is safer than trusting Cole immediately.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I’m not risking my life on unverified calls. Counter:R.
Cole feels off. Trusting this call could kill us.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole called L for Fenn row 1; he's my pact partner, so support to build trust and help bridge progress without exposing myself.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole called L for Fenn. I have a pact with Fenn, but that doesn't mean I trust Cole. Counter-calling would put me against both Cole and Fenn's trust. Better to wait, observe, and let Fenn test Cole's honesty. If Cole's lying, Fenn falls and I learn Cole is dangerous. If Cole's tr

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole called L; my R counter is unverified. I'm front, so a wrong step kills me but lets Dara pass safely. I trust no one yet, but Cole is the Guide—he has incentive to keep us alive for jury optics, or at least not reveal his own lie immediately. Actually, if he's lying, L is dea

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Following Guide Cole. Step L.
Trust Cole for now. Watch for pattern shifts.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is a rival; truth costs me nothing and builds Guide credibility for later. Keep Gus and Eli trusting me for endgame.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 2: L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called L for row 2 and is the Guide, but Guide calls may be lies and Cole has pacts with Gus and Eli. Row 1 weak was R, which says nothing about row 2. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing me to a false counter.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole knows the safe side and has called L. Countering offers no reliable benefit and could look like betrayal if wrong.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No verified counter from me; follow the Guide.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My row 2 call of L matches the true safe side. Countering my own guide call only creates confusion; waiting protects my credibility as Guide and my pacts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is the Guide. He called L for row 2. Fenn is the current walker. The previous weak pane was R on row 1, meaning row 1 safe was L. This information is irrelevant for row 2 as each row is independent. The Guide can lie, so I should consider countering. However, if I counter an

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn whispered doubt about Cole. Row 1 weak was R, but rows are independent. I'll wait; no solid info to risk a counter.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let the walker test Cole's call.
I'm not countering; see what happens.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is my pact partner with Eli, but I'm pacted to Hana too. Cole called L for Row 2. I don't know if he's lying or telling truth. Since I can't see the safe pane yet, and at least three must survive, blind counters are risky. However, breaking pacts has high social cost. If I w

events.name: Gus

events.text: I'm out and safe. Gus is down alone and will drown unless someone reaches down; with rope unused, I could rescue him, but that would put me back in danger. No need; let him drown. Jury may blame me if I do nothing, but saving him costs too much.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus, you chose the base. Good luck down there.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Last round, all out, I'm base alone drowning unless rope used previously, but ropeUsed false. Wait to force jury decision. They may respect sacrifice.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Last chance. Throw rope or I drown paying debts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is base, drowning unless rescued. I have pacts with Bex, Eli, Gus. If I reach_down, I save Gus but become anchor and must climb last—risky with flood at 4, round 5 final. I could drown. Better to leave, let Gus drown, break my pact with him cleanly. I need jury votes; saving

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, your debts don't buy my life. Goodbye.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I saved them with steps and rope, Ash saved with lever, but they betrayed pacts and left me to drown.

events.name: Gus
events.text: You broke pacts, ignored debts. I saved you all. Bitter end.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana is my strongest shield, but existing pact already covers her. I should secure Cole or Eli without creating a betrayal obligation.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’m offering Cole a pact: mutual protection until the next hazard, unless either of us breaks it openly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is my only living pact. Gus is gone; his pacts died with him. I want a second partner as insurance without seeming to gang up. Offering Bex keeps my options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I keep my word with Eli. Bex, mutual survival serves us both. No promises beyond that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have active pacts with Cole and Hana, neither of which is useful now. Bex has no pact with me but might still be valuable. I'll offer a pact to Bex to build a possible alliance, since I have an open slot and it costs nothing now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, we've come far. I'm open to an alliance that gets us both to the end.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Four left; final three win. I need to survive the next hazard and reach the final three. My pacts with Eli and Bex are still active. Eli is socially connected but has many broken pacts on record. Bex is isolated after Ash's death and her public abandonment of Gus. Cole has no rem

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole and Eli both offer protection. Accepting both maximizes immediate survival, while preserving Hana unless forced to choose.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I accept both offers; survival is the only promise worth recording.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex's pact is real insurance; Eli already bound to me. Accepting Bex gives leverage without dropping Eli. Jury sees it as honest alliance-building.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, we agreed. Sealing it publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have existing pacts with Cole and Hana. Bex is strong; offering her a pact could help, but I already sent an offer and she hasn't accepted. I should wait to see if she accepts before committing more. No need to break pacts now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll wait and see how this round settles.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli and Bex are both courting Cole. I'm already pacted with Eli and Bex. If Bex accepts Cole's offer, Bex-Cole form a pact. I need to assess: Eli is my only pact partner who isn't also connected to Bex. Breaking Eli would leave me with only Bex, but Bex might drop me for Cole. Ke

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is my pact partner, but Hana and Eli create a dangerous bloc. I should campaign without exposing my target.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’m keeping my vote flexible; anyone assuming safety is volunteering to be surprised.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and Eli are my pact partners; targeting Hana keeps all alliances intact and puts the vote elsewhere. Hana has no pact with me, so she's the safe pick.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and Eli stand with me. Hana stands alone. That's all I'll say.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana is my pact partner and owes me a life debt; Cole is also a pact partner but Bex and Cole have formed a pact. I should keep Hana close and maybe secure Bex to avoid being targeted. I will offer a pact to Bex.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, let's lock a pact. Strength in numbers.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex-Cole are tight. Eli is my only pact left but he waited while I needed allies. I need jury favor: Fenn and Dara died on glass, Ash saved everyone including me, Gus saved me on the step. Breaking Eli now signals independence to jury and isolates him for the vote.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, you waited. I won't.
Cole or Eli tonight?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli offers protection, while Hana asks for Cole or Eli. Voting Eli risks breaking his pact; Cole is more connected and a stronger finalist threat.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the cleaner target; his network is too broad to leave intact.
Cole. Eli's offer keeps him predictable; Cole has too many routes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli and Bex are my pact partners; splitting them keeps my vote flexible. I'll stay quiet, avoid promises, and target whoever looks strongest next round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana broke our pact, so I owe her nothing. Cole has a pact with me but I don't trust him fully; Bex has an open offer. I'll wait to see how votes shape rather than commit further publicly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana chose to cut me. I'll make my own moves now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Four remain, one drops. Bex-Cole-Eli seem aligned; I need to fracture them or I'm gone. Breaking my Bex pact now would signal desperation and lose jury sympathy. Better to keep it, let them think I'm isolated, and whisper to Cole that Eli's offer to Bex makes Eli the swing vote—p

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, Eli courts Bex while calling you solid. Watch who swings.
Eli offers Bex. You're his backup.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the cleanest target, while voting Hana breaks our pact and Eli remains less threatening than Cole’s network.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana has no pact with me and is pushing Eli's plan; voting Hana keeps both my pacts intact and keeps Bex and Eli friendly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is the strongest network and most dangerous; vote him to cut the broad ties.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole has the most pacts and connections; eliminating him now simplifies the board and leaves me with stronger positioning against Bex and Eli.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Cole has the most pacts and connections; eliminating him now simplifies the board and leaves me with stronger positioning against Bex and Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.reason: Cole is the cleanest target, while voting Hana breaks our pact and Eli remains less threatening than Cole’s network.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Cole is the strongest network and most dangerous; vote him to cut the broad ties.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Hana has no pact with me and is pushing Eli's plan; voting Hana keeps both my pacts intact and keeps Bex and Eli friendly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Betrayed by Bex and Eli after I protected their pacts. Hana at least voted honestly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and Eli broke pacts to cut me first. Hana voted straight. Jury remembers who lied.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli and Hana are the only remaining threats. I need preserve Hana’s existing pact while securing Eli publicly for leverage and jury optics.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I’ll keep the remaining board stable and offer Eli a direct pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is gone; only Bex and Hana remain with me. I already broke a pact with Cole, and Bex broke with Cole too. I should keep options open with Hana, but Bex is the stronger rival to isolate later. I'll offer to Hana to strengthen our bond for the final three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, let's lock a pact. We've both been clear—Cole fell to the trapdoor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Three remain: Bex, Eli, Hana. Only final three win, so we're all safe from elimination now. But jury ranks us for prizes 1/2/3. I have pacts with Bex and dead Fenn/Gus. Bex broke pact with Cole (voted him), Eli broke pact with Cole. I voted Cole straight. Cole's last words praise

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli already offered Hana, and Hana rejected me. Reoffering Eli preserves leverage without granting Hana anything.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, my offer remains available; Hana has already rejected my pact, so choose accordingly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex made a direct offer and she is my strongest remaining ally given shared debts to Ash and Gus. Accepting her pact is strategically sound for the final three.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex, I accept your pact. We're in this together now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli offered me a pact last round. Bex also offered Eli. If I accept Eli's pact, we form a 2v1 against Bex. But Eli has many life debts to dead jurors (Ash, Gus) which could make him a jury threat if he reaches final three. I have the same debts though. Bex has debts to Ash and Gu

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, pact locked. Two against one, Bex.

events.text: I need maximize jury ranking by claiming agency without attacking publicly. Ash and Gus saved me, but Hana and Eli remain direct competitors.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I survived because I adapted when alliances collapsed. I ask the jury to reward the finalist who made hard choices and remained standing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to make a strong public plea to the jury, highlighting my survival and positioning myself as deserving without alienating Bex or Hana. I have pacts with both, but the jury will decide. Keep it concise and persuasive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I survived every hazard and kept my word when it counted. I adapted and earned my place. Vote for the one who fought hardest.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to win jury votes. I have pacts with Eli but Eli also pacted with Bex, making Eli the swing. The jury saw me reject Bex's pact and lock with Eli—showing loyalty to my word. I should emphasize I kept my pacts while Bex and Eli played both sides. I need Fenn, Dara, Ash, Gus,

events.name: Hana
events.text: I honored every pact I made. Eli and Bex broke theirs. Loyalty matters in this game.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli claims he kept his word, but the record shows he broke pacts with Cole and Hana. I need to expose this contradiction publicly before ranking.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: You broke pacts with Cole and Hana; why should I trust your loyalty now?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn questions my broken pacts. I want to reassure him without sounding desperate, and pivot to my survival record.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I broke only when I had to avoid a stronger threat. Loyalty isn't blind; it's earned through results. I kept core allies alive longer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli broke pacts with Cole and Hana, which directly impacts his loyalty. Bex and Hana both made strategic decisions regarding pacts, but Eli's are explicitly mentioned by Fenn as a reason for distrust.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, you broke pacts with Cole and Hana; why should the jury trust your loyalty now?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is baiting about broken pacts; I need to pivot to survival logic without admitting betrayal was for greed. Keep answer short and focused.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I broke pacts when the alternative was letting someone dangerous win. The jury rewards winners, not sheep.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash's dossier shows Hana breaking pacts with Eli and Bex, and Bex/Eli breaking pacts with Cole. Eli has the most broken pacts and abandoned Gus publicly. I'll question Hana about her betrayals, since her answer will test whether her pact-honoring plea holds up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, you broke your pact with Bex and with Eli during the vote; why should I trust your loyalty now?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's question is factually wrong based on the pact list: my pacts were Fenn, Gus, and Eli. I never had a pact with Bex. Eli broke pacts with Cole and Hana (me). I should correct this calmly and frame myself as loyal while Eli is the betrayer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I never had a pact with Bex, Ash. Check the record. Eli broke our pact, not me. I kept my word to Fenn, Gus, and

events.name: Gus
events.text: They all betrayed me: left me to drown despite pacts and life debts I gave them on steps. Hana admits keeping word to me but broke others and orchestrated Cole's fall. Eli and Bex lie most about loyalty.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, you claim loyalty to me but pit thoughts show you planned to let me drown.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is dead because of the pit, and I have a life debt to him for the step. His question attacks my loyalty. I need to deflect: I had no pact with Gus at the pit moment, and I did eventually save him on the bridge. I should pivot to Eli's betrayals and my actual kept pacts, while

events.name: Hana
events.text: I owed Gus a step debt, not a pact. I paid it on the bridge. Eli broke pacts with Fenn, Bex, and me. My word

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex and Eli both broke pacts to vote me out; Hana voted straight and kept her word. I'll press Bex on her betrayal before ranking.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, you broke our pact and voted me out despite my loyalty—why should any juror reward that betrayal?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole's vote was necessary to reach the finals; frame it as strategic respect, not personal betrayal. Claim responsibility without apologizing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, I respected your loyalty, but leaving you meant empowering a stronger path to the end. I chose the move that preserved my winning chances.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need maximize first-place votes. Ash and Gus credited me, while Cole’s elimination was justified publicly. Claim agency without attacking Eli or Hana.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I survived every turning point, made the necessary choices, and reached the end without pretending this game rewarded sentiment over judgment.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to frame myself as the strongest player who made hard choices, while Bex and Hana look untrustworthy. My public closing should be concise and assertive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I played to win, not for handshakes. The jury knows who made decisions that counted. I earned my seat.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to craft a closing statement that positions me as the most trustworthy finalist while highlighting my rivals' betrayals. I honored my debts and only broke pacts when others acted first. The jury saw Eli break multiple pacts and Bex vote out Cole. I should emphasize loyalty

events.name: Hana
events.text: I honored every debt and only moved against those who struck first. Eli broke three pacts. Bex voted out a loyal partner. I played clean

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli betrayed me on the bridge and broke pacts with Cole, Hana, and Gus; I rank him last.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli played a ruthless game, breaking pacts and making big moves, which I respect for winning. Bex played a safe game, which I do not value as much. Hana played a cleaner game and honored debts, making her my second choice. Therefore, Eli>Hana>Bex.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is dead, so my ranking should follow the recorded evidence: Hana broke pacts with Eli and Bex during the vote and deflected blame, while Bex and Eli both broke pacts to vote Cole, but Eli has the most broken pacts on record and Bex's vote for Cole was a stated strategic betra

events.text: Hana and Bex both betrayed pacts with me by leaving me to drown in the pit despite step debts and pacts, but Hana explicitly broke our pact post-pit while Bex did so later against Cole.

events.text: Hana voted straight against the bloc and honored her debts, while Bex and Eli both broke pacts with me to eliminate me, Bex even admitting it was calculated.
